# Play one playlist everywhere with Alexa+

> **In short:** With Alexa+ you can set up a voice routine so a single phrase — like "Alexa, play my dinner playlist" — starts the same music in every room at once. It uses the Alexa app's Routines feature.

Imagine saying "Alexa, play my dinner playlist" and the same music starts in the kitchen, lounge and bedroom at once. You'll learn how to set up one playlist that plays across multiple rooms with a single voice command.

## Before you start
- An **Amazon account** (free).
- The **Alexa app** installed on your phone or tablet (Android or iOS).
- At least one **Amazon Echo device** (like an Echo Dot, Echo Show or Echo Studio) in each room.
- A **music streaming service** already linked to Alexa (Amazon Music, Spotify, Apple Music, etc.).
- Roughly **15 minutes** of your time.

---

## Step 1 — Open the Alexa app and go to Devices
Open the Alexa app on your phone or tablet. At the bottom of the screen you'll see a row of icons — look for the one that looks like a **house outline** (this is the Devices section). Tap it. You should see a list of all your Echo devices, often grouped by room.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows your rooms and devices.

💬 **Example:** Look for the house-shaped icon at the bottom of the Alexa app and tap it.

---

## Step 2 — Pick a room to start
Choose the room where you want the music to begin. Tap the room name (for example, "Kitchen"). Inside that room view, look for a menu option — this is typically a **three-dot menu (⋯)** in the top-right corner, though on some app versions it may appear as a **gear icon** or a **menu with three lines** instead.

You'll know it worked when a menu slides up or opens from the bottom of the screen.

💬 **Example:** Open the Kitchen room and look for the ⋯ menu in the top-right corner.

---

## Step 3 — Find the routine option in the menu
From the menu that just appeared, look for an option to add this room to a routine — the exact wording may be **"Add to Routine"** or something similar depending on your app version. Tap it.

If you're not sure which option it is, look for any menu item that mentions "routine" or "routine" in English — this is the feature that links your voice phrase to your music action.

You'll know it worked when a routine setup screen opens.

💬 **Example:** Tap **Add to Routine** (or the equivalent option in your app version).

---

## Step 4 — Choose a voice trigger
In the routine setup screen, look for the option to set a **voice trigger** — on many versions this is labeled **"Voice"** and shown with a microphone icon. Tap it. A text box appears where you can type the phrase you want to say to Alexa to start the playlist.

If the voice option isn't visible, look through the list of available trigger types for something related to speaking or voice commands.

You'll know it worked when you see a text box labeled something like "Enter your phrase" and a way to confirm and move to the next step.

💬 **Example:** Tap the voice trigger option and then tap inside the text box.

---

## Step 5 — Type your wake-up phrase
Type a short phrase you'll say to Alexa, for example:
💬 **"Alexa, play dinner playlist"**

Confirm the phrase and move to the next step. Alexa may show a summary of the phrase you've entered.

You'll know it worked when the summary confirms your exact phrase.

💬 **Example:** Type "Alexa, play dinner playlist" and confirm it.

---

## Step 6 — Add the music action
In the routine setup, look for an action type related to music — this may be labeled **"Music"** (often with a musical note icon) or something similar depending on your app version. Tap it. A new screen opens where you can pick the playlist and the devices that should play it.

If you don't see a music option right away, look through the list of available actions for anything about playing audio or music.

You'll know it worked when you see options to choose a playlist and to choose which devices or rooms should play it.

💬 **Example:** Tap the music action and then tap the option to choose a playlist.

---

## Step 7 — Pick your playlist and devices
Select the playlist you want to play everywhere. Then choose all the rooms where you want the music to play (for example, Kitchen, Lounge, Bedroom) — look for a device or room picker. Save the routine.

You'll know it worked when the routine summary shows your chosen playlist and all the rooms you selected.

💬 **Example:** Select "Dinner Vibes" playlist and tick Kitchen, Lounge and Bedroom.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Wrong room selected** — If the music only plays in one room, double-check Step 2 and make sure you picked the correct room before saving the routine.
- **Phrase already used** — If Alexa says the phrase is taken, add a word like "my" or change the wording slightly (for example, "Alexa, start dinner playlist").
- **Device not selected** — If a room is missing, go back to Step 7 and make sure every room is ticked before saving.

---

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Set up a "Good morning" routine that plays your favorite news podcast in the bedroom and kitchen at the same time.
- **For your business or work:** Create a "Focus time" routine that plays lo-fi beats in every meeting room whenever you say "Alexa, start focus time".
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one room and one playlist; once it works, add more rooms in the same routine.

---

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, go to Devices, pick a room, tap the menu icon → look for a routine option → choose voice trigger → type your phrase → add a music action → pick your playlist and devices → Save. Say the phrase out loud to test it.
